title: Contractible comma categories imply coherent cofinal restriction
statement:
Use the universes, infinite regular cardinals, small simplicial sets and filtered quasicategories of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent functors, cocones, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $u:I\to J$ be a coherent functor of small quasicategories. For $j\in J$, let $J_{j/}$ be the coherent category of arrows $j\to j'$, with commuting triangles and higher compatibilities, and let
$$I_{j/}=I\times^h_J J_{j/}.$$
Here an object is $(i,a:j\to u(i))$, with coherent commuting triangles and all higher compatibilities, so the pullback is the infinity-categorical pullback. Suppose that $I_{j/}$ is weakly contractible for every $j$, meaning that its space obtained by inverting all arrows is contractible. Then for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a sufficiently large universe, coherent diagram $H:J\to\mathcal E$ and vertex $T\in\mathcal E$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_J T)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(Hu,\Delta_I T).$$
It is natural in $H,T$ and compatible with coherent postcomposition. Restriction also gives an equivalence of coherent cocone quasicategories $\mathcal E_{H/}\to\mathcal E_{Hu/}$ over $\mathcal E$, where the projection records the cocone vertex. Consequently any given cocone on $H$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction is, with the same vertex. No colimit-existence assumption on $\mathcal E$ is needed.

source.place: HTT (April 9, 2017), Theorem 4.1.3.1, Proposition 4.1.1.7 and Proposition 4.1.1.8; contractible comma criterion and the actual restriction equivalences. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Choose a universe $\mathcal W$ containing $I,J,\mathcal E$ and all the mapping spaces used below, and form its space category in a further universe. Put $v=u^{\mathrm{op}}:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to J^{\mathrm{op}}$. The opposite operation gives quasicategories and identifies $(v\downarrow j)$ with the opposite of the arrow-comma model $I_{j/}$. This can be read simplex by simplex: $(i,\alpha:u^{\mathrm{op}}i\to j)$ corresponds to $(i,\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}:j\to u i)$, with every triangle and higher simplex reversed. To justify the pullback model, apply the isofibration-exponentiation theorem to $J\to *$ and $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$: the endpoint map $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,J)\to J\times J$ is an isofibration. Pulling back along $k\mapsto(j,k)$ gives the source-fixed arrow projection $J_{j/}\to J$. Isofibrations are preserved by these pullbacks: an inner-horn lifting problem, or a specified-source equivalence lifting problem, projects to one upstairs, and its lift pairs with the prescribed base simplex or equivalence. The isofibration-pullback-limit theorem therefore identifies the strict simplicial pullback $I\times_J J_{j/}$ with the infinity-categorical pullback in the hypothesis. Opposite reversal identifies its opposite degree by degree with the child's displayed arrow-comma model $(v\downarrow j)$. Reversal preserves weak contractibility: on realizations the map reverses the order of barycentric coordinates on each simplex, respecting face and degeneracy relations. Hence every $(v\downarrow j)$ is weakly contractible. No filteredness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1; comma orientation and passage to opposites; online source, not archived in literature/; expanded argument by NP; categorical pullback justification: Kerodon Corollary 4.5.3.28 (033R), via the cited isofibration-pullback-limit node

proof.text: Apply pointwise space-valued left Kan extension to $v$ and $\Delta_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}*$. Denote the result by $L$, its unit by $\eta$, and let $e:L\to\Delta_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}*$ be the mate of the identity of $\Delta_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}*$. Its component $e_j$ is the canonical map from the colimit of the constant point indexed by $(v\downarrow j)$ to the point. Spaces have all the required small colimits. The weakly-contractible constant-diagram assertion of lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula, applied with $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ and $X=*$, says exactly that each $e_j$ is an equivalence. The pointwise criterion for equivalences in a coherent functor category now makes $e$ an equivalence.

source.place: Sections 4.3.2-4.3.3 and Proposition 4.3.3.7; pointwise calculation of the mate; online source, not archived in literature/; expanded argument by NP

proof.text:
For any $F:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$, precomposition with $e$ and the Kan-extension adjunction give equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}(\Delta_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}*,F)\xrightarrow{e^*}\operatorname{Map}(L,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}(\Delta_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}*,Fv).$$
By the adjunction formula, the composite map sends $\alpha:\Delta_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}*\to F$ to $(\alpha v)(ev)\eta$. The mate correspondence supplies a coherent homotopy $(ev)\eta\simeq\operatorname{id}$, because $e$ is the mate of that identity. Postcomposition by $\alpha v$ gives a homotopy to $\alpha v$, natural in $\alpha$ and all its higher simplices. Thus the composite map is homotopic to restriction itself, so restriction is an equivalence of spaces. Under the dual transport classification of right fibrations, the constant point is represented by $J\xrightarrow{1}J$. For every right fibration $q:X\to J$, the displayed mapping spaces are therefore the spaces of sections $\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(J,X)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}_{/J}(I,X)$, respectively. Compatibility of transport with pullback and composition identifies their comparison with the actual section restriction.

source.place: Definition 4.1.1.1, with Proposition 4.3.3.7; computation of the actual restriction map; online source, not archived in literature/; expanded argument by NP

proof.text: For $T\in\mathcal E$, the source map $Q_T=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal E}\{T\}\to\mathcal E$ is a right fibration. Pull back along $H$; right horn lifting is preserved by pullback, because a lifting square in the pullback is exactly a lifting square upstairs with its prescribed base. Apply step 3 to this right fibration over $J$. By currying simplicial maps, its section space is exactly the arrow mapping space $U_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_J T)$, and the analogous space over $I$ is $U_{\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal E)}(Hu,\Delta_I T)$. The natural right-pinch inclusions identify these with the specified right-pinched mapping spaces. Their naturality makes a commuting square with section restriction, so two-out-of-three gives precisely the mapping-space restriction asserted in the item.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.1.7; section interpretation of cocone spaces and mapping-model comparison; online source, not archived in literature/; expanded argument by NP

proof.text: The cocone projections $\mathcal E_{H/}\to\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E_{Hu/}\to\mathcal E$ are left fibrations. Indeed the source-fixed arrow projection in $D=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)$ is the opposite of the target-fixed right fibration for $D^{\mathrm{op}}$; reversing the horn index converts right lifting to left lifting. Pull it back along $\Delta_J:\mathcal E\to D$ to obtain exactly the cocone category in the definition; do the same for $I$. Restriction is a map of these left fibrations over the identity of $\mathcal E$. Their fibers at $T$ are the arrow mapping spaces in step 4, so its fiber maps are equivalences. Under transport classification this map is a transformation between the classifying space-valued functors whose components are those fiber maps. The componentwise criterion makes it an equivalence. Full faithfulness of transport then supplies an inverse over $\mathcal E$ with the inverse homotopies; forgetting the base gives the claimed equivalence of cocone quasicategories. The base stays the identity, so the vertex is unchanged.

source.place: Propositions 4.1.1.7-4.1.1.8; passage from fiber equivalences to cocone-category equivalence; online source, not archived in literature/; expanded argument by NP

proof.text: Let $\lambda:H\to\Delta_J L_0$ be any given cocone. For each $T$, the colimit criterion tests whether $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(L_0,T)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal E)}(H,\Delta_J T)$, $a\mapsto\Delta_J(a)\lambda$, is an equivalence. The criterion for the restricted cocone has the same source and the target with $I$ in place of $J$. Restriction composes the first test map to the second, and its target comparison is an equivalence by step 4. Two-out-of-three proves both implications for this particular cocone. Naturality in $H$ is precomposition by a coherent transformation, and naturality in $T$ is postcomposition by its constant transformation. These operations commute with restriction as simplicial maps. For a coherent functor $P:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$, the equation $P(\lambda|_I)=(P\lambda)|_I$ holds on every simplex; the pinch comparisons are natural under $P$, so the claimed compatibility with coherent postcomposition also holds. All colimits introduced in the proof were in spaces; none in $\mathcal E$ was assumed.
